Meta Description Generator

Generate concise, search-engine-ready meta descriptions directly in your browser without creating an account.

How the Meta Description Generator works

Type the main topic of your web page into the field labeled What the page is about. Next, enter your primary search terms in the Target keywords field, separating multiple phrases with commas. Select your preferred output size from the Length dropdown menu, choosing either short for concise snippets or long for detailed summaries. Finally, set a Minimum words threshold to ensure the generated text provides enough context for searchers.

The generator creates a search-ready snippet that combines a benefit-driven lead sentence, key differentiators like speed or privacy, and your specified keywords. It automatically trims the output to stay under 160 characters without cutting words in half. You can copy the generated text directly into your site's HTML or content management system.

Formula used

template: lead sentence + differentiator + privacy line, trimmed to ≤ 160 chars

SymbolMeaning
leadyour topic restated as a benefit
differentiatorwhat makes the page worth the click — speed, privacy, no signup
trimcut at the last sentence boundary that fits, never mid-word

A good description does not rank the page — Google rewrites most snippets — but it decides whether searchers click yours instead of a competitor’s. Front-load the actual topic and keep it one clean sentence plus one reason to click.

Inputs used: What the page is about, Target keywords (comma separated), Length, Minimum words.

Worked example

Here is how to generate a snippet using a sample blog tool topic.

  • Enter 'keyword density checker for blog posts' into the topic field.
  • Add 'keyword density, seo writing' as your target keywords and select 'short' for length.
  • Set the minimum word count to 25 and click generate to receive a 159-character meta description.

Result:

  • description: Keyword density checker for blog posts — fast, free and private. Works on any device, right in the browser — keyword density checker for blog posts in seconds.
  • chars: 159
  • words: 28

Frequently asked questions

What is the character limit for a meta description?
Search engines typically truncate meta descriptions longer than 155 to 160 characters on desktop devices and roughly 120 characters on mobile. Keeping your snippet around 150 characters prevents your text from being cut off in search results.
How many target keywords should I include in a meta description?
Include one or two relevant keywords naturally within the text. Stuffing too many keywords harms readability and can cause search engines to ignore your snippet entirely.
Does Google always use the meta description I write?
No, Google often rewrites meta descriptions based on the user's specific search query. However, providing a clear, accurate description increases the chances that search engines use your text.
What formula does the Meta Description Generator use?
It uses template: lead sentence + differentiator + privacy line, trimmed to ≤ 160 chars, where lead is the your topic restated as a benefit; differentiator is the what makes the page worth the click — speed, privacy, no signup; trim is the cut at the last sentence boundary that fits, never mid-word.
How do I read the result?
A good description does not rank the page — Google rewrites most snippets — but it decides whether searchers click yours instead of a competitor’s. Front-load the actual topic and keep it one clean sentence plus one reason to click.
